reply_text:
The loop is running on all four seats. I'm now setting up a wake-up for the one-hour check, because the first way I tried fired immediately.㊥ Gist: The backfill is running for an hour on four seats, one Kimi and three Codex, with no Sonnet. Each job is a pack of ten turns. I will check quality when the hour is up, about 21:55 UTC.

㊢ (what is running) A new script, `scripts/backfill_loop.py` (commit 5ab71a4a), runs as the user unit `xiang-backfill-loop`. Each seat loops through five steps:
1. Claim ten unread turns.
2. Build a pack.
3. Dispatch it.
4. Wait for the job, then publish through the validator.
5. Log one line to `storage/operator-turns/backfill-loop.jsonl`.

The seats are kimi-3, codex-9, codex-4 and codex-6, and all four are working on their first pack. No new pack starts after 60 minutes, and jobs already running are waited for. A turn gets at most two tries. To stop early, create `/tmp/claude17/backfill-loop.STOP`.

㊢ (which turns) The loop first takes the 63 turns left in the 1 to 21 August block, then July. The August 22 onwards blocks already have older readings, so the next unread months are July and earlier. I built three July blocks of 100 turns. At about seven minutes a pack, four seats should read 250 to 300 turns this hour, so that is enough.

㊟ (limits of this run)
- **No second readings:** the one-in-ten reread is not in this run, so there is no agreement figure yet.
- **Refused turns are only logged,** not sent back to the reader. They come round once more in a later pack.
- **Codex usage:** the weekly window read 84% used this afternoon. Three Codex seats for an hour may hit the limit. Failed jobs would show up in the log as errors, and the Kimi seat would carry on.

㊢ (check at the hour) Park `park-a1a8a998-5311-453e-a7e1-b47255ad8041` is a timer that wakes me at 21:55 UTC. It is not tied to a job. I will then report, for each seat:
- packs, turns published and refused, and minutes per pack;
- the mechanical check on each block;
- three records read in full, one Kimi and two Codex, with every citation in them checked against its pattern;
- a 小象 edition logged.

㊥ Gist: This wake-up is a stray and not the hour check. It came from the first park I tried, which had nothing to wait on and so fired at once. The loop has been running for one minute. All four seats are on their first pack, and nothing has been logged yet.

㊢ (state) The unit `xiang-backfill-loop` is active. The real hour check is park `park-a1a8a998-5311-453e-a7e1-b47255ad8041`, which wakes me at about 21:55 UTC. I am taking no action until then.

㊥ Gist: The hour produced about 340 new readings from four seats, with segments and intents in good shape. But Codex cites patterns far too readily, on 50% to 97% of fragments, and the two Codex citations I read were a stretch and a word-match error. Before running further, I propose to tighten citations and filter out non-operator turns.

㊢ (throughput) The loop stopped by itself at 21:50.

| Seat | Packs | Turns published | Refused | Minutes per pack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| codex-4 | 12 | 103 | 8 | 3.7 |
| codex-6 | 14 | 96 | 24 | 3.8 |
| codex-9 | 13 | 93 | 18 | 3.4 |
| kimi-3 | 6 | 50 | 0 | 9.9 |

- **Refusals:** mostly relation labels in the packs built before that fix. One Kimi pack was lost to a compaction and then redone.
- **Blocks:** the three July blocks are 100, 99 and 100 of 100 published. The 1 to 21 August block is at 87 of 100.

㊩ (Codex citations) Share of fragments with a citation, by reader:

| Reader | Citation rate |
|---|---|
| codex-4, codex-6, codex-9 | 52% to 97% per block |
| kimi-3 | 17% to 39% |
| Earlier readers | 13% to 20% |

What I found reading citations against their patterns:
- **Wrong:** `exotic/full-lift-registry`, about a registry of Lisp lift rules, is cited for your "cross-references to the full files in the metadata". The only link is the word "metadata".
- **A stretch:** `contracts/rebase-by-name`, about anchoring pointers by name rather than line number, is cited for your "Not quite, you can see Cooked for 8s on line 8433". Your move is correcting where the agent thinks something appears.
- **Plausible:** `library-coherence/library-template-discipline` for keeping template-compliant abstracts.

When every sentence arrives with pattern hits already attached, Codex treats a hit as a fit. The segments and intents in the same records read correctly.

㊩ (non-operator text) The Kimi record I drew was the harness's own auto-resume message ("You were auto-resumed. In ONE line, confirm…"), read as if it were you. Together with the three copies of one whole transcript, this shows the July blocks include turns whose origin was never matched. The August blocks exclude those.

㊢ (小象 edition 7) Accuracy 0.377 and macro F1 0.219 over 4,020 turns. That is up slightly, but it includes the harness turns.

㊭ (changes before the next run)
1. Leave out turns whose origin is unmatched, and very long turns. I will also mark this hour's harness-text readings so 小象 skips them.
2. Treat citations as unverified when they arrive. A cheap second pass by Kimi would check citations only, pattern text beside fragment, and keep or drop each.
3. Change the pack rule so a citation must name the pattern's IF condition that your turn meets.
4. The checker flags any reader whose citation rate is above 40% for a pack.
5. Run again for an hour with Codex as the main reader, then compare citation rates and read a sample.

The segments and intents from this hour can go to 小象 as they are. The citations should not go into the pattern graph until step 2 has checked them.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I make changes 1 to 4 and start the next hour?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Yes, they can be batched. The time goes on tool calls, about 67 per turn, not on judgement, so I have dispatched a builder that fetches everything in advance and lets a reader do ten turns in one pass.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (where the four minutes go) For each fragment the reader runs two pattern searches, then opens each plausible pattern file to read its IF and THEN, then fills a template, validates and publishes. Each of those steps is a separate round trip to the model. Codex's one record took 67 tool calls. The other readers were faster per record, 1.2 to 1.5 minutes, but by the same method.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the batched version: `scripts/backfill_pack.py`, zai-1)
- **`pack`** builds one file for ten turns. It holds:
  - each turn's text with sentence ids and offsets, plus the two previous turns of the same session as context;
  - move hits and subject hits for every sentence, with every pattern of a family the turn names;
  - an appendix giving each distinct pattern's conclusion, context, IF, HOWEVER and THEN once.
- The reader reads that one file and returns one JSON array covering all ten turns, with no tool calls. If nothing in the pack fits a turn, it can name up to three extra searches for a second round.
- **`publish`** validates and publishes each turn separately through the existing validator. A bad turn is refused on its own and the rest still publish. Nothing is ever overwritten.
- Job: `invoke-1790789698242-29257-4d26bd96`
- Park: `park-878c58ef-71ce-4a2c-903f-0624b935ccb4`

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what batching trades away) A reader can only judge the patterns the search surfaced, which is why the pack carries subject hits and whole named families as well as move hits. The "no generator scripts" rule stays. It was there to stop a reader writing analyses by program without reading, and here the reader still writes every analysis itself.
